facts.text: The MRT is clean, cheap, and extensive enough to reach nearly every tourist area directly; an EZ-Link card taps onto trains and buses alike, and Changi Airport itself is worth budgeting time for as a first-day activity.

A hawker centre meal runs roughly S$5-10 (~$4-7); a mid-range hotel is closer to S$150-250/night (~$110-185) — the gap between eating well at a hawker centre and a proper sit-down restaurant is large, not marginal.

Hawker stalls directly facing Chinatown's or Clarke Quay's main tourist strips are often marked up compared to equally good stalls a few stalls or streets over (Maxwell Food Centre and neighborhood centres tend to be both cheaper and more authentic).
Gardens by the Bay and Marina Bay Sands SkyPark sell timed tickets, and sunset slots sell out — book ahead rather than assuming walk-up entry.
Laws around chewing gum import, littering, and jaywalking are genuinely enforced with real fines, not just reputation; the climate is hot and humid essentially year-round.
Hawker centres typically have dedicated halal-certified and vegetarian stalls side by side, making Singapore one of the easier major cities to eat well regardless of dietary restriction.
